1 # Checkpoint Engine 2 Checkpoint-engine is a simple middleware to update model weights in LLM inference engines -- a critical step in reinforcement learning. 3 We provide an efficient and lightweight implementation for inplace weight update: 4 updating our [Kimi-K2](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K2) model (1 Trillion parameters) across thousands of GPUs takes about 20s. 5 6 7
8 9 10 11
12 13 ## Architecture 14 15 The core weight update logic is in `ParameterServer` class, a service colocated with inference engines. It provides two implementations of weight update: Broadcast and P2P. 16 17 - **Broadcast**: Used when a large number of inference instances need to update weights in synchronous. This is the fastest implementation and should be used as the default update method. See `_update_per_bucket` with `ranks == None or []`. 18 - **P2P**: Used when new inference instances are dynamically added (due to restarts or dynamic availability) while the existing instances are already serving requests. Under this scenario, to avoid affecting the workloads on existing instances, we use the [`mooncake-transfer-engine`](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake?tab=readme-ov-file#use-python-package) to P2P send weights from CPUs in existing instances to GPUs in new instances. See `_update_per_bucket` with `ranks` specified. 19 20 ### Optimized Weight Broadcast 21 In the *Broadcast* implementation, the checkpoint-engine holds references to sharded weights in CPU memory, and need to efficiently broadcast them to a cluster of inference instances, often under a different sharding pattern. 22 We arrange the data transfer into 3 stages: 23 1. H2D: moving weights to GPU memory. These weights may come from disk or the training engine. 24 2. broadcast: broadcast among checkpoint engine workers; the data results in a CUDA IPC buffer shared with inference engine. 25 3. reload: inference engine decides what subset of weights to copy from the broadcasted data. 26 27 Checkpoint-engine orchestrates the entire transfer process. It first gathers necessary metadata to create a plan, including deciding the proper bucket size for data transfer. 28 It then executes the transfer, where it controls the inference engine through a ZeroMQ socket. To maximize performance, it organizes the data transfers into a pipeline with overlapped communication and copy, illustrated below. The details can be found in [Kimi-K2 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534). 29 30 31
32 33 34 35
36 37 Pipelining naturally requires more GPU memory. When memory is not enough, checkpoint-engine will fallback to serial execution. 38 39 ### Optimized P2P Bucket Assignment 40 In the *P2P* implementation, checkpoint-engine needs to send weights from existing instances to new instances. 41 To minimize the overall transfer time, checkpoint-engine optimizes the bucket assignment for each sender-receiver pair. 42 The optimization goal is to make full use of the available network bandwidth for each sender and receiver. 43 See [issue #25](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine/issues/25) 44 45 ## Benchmark 46 47 | Model | Device Info | GatherMetas | Update (Broadcast) | Update (P2P) | 48 | :----------------------------------- | :----------- | :---------- |:-------------------| :---------------------- | 49 | GLM-4.5-Air (BF16) | 8xH800 TP8 | 0.12s | 3.47s (3.02GiB) | 4.12s (3.02GiB) | 50 | Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 (BF16) | 8xH800 TP8 | 0.33s | 6.22s (2.67GiB) | 7.10s (2.68GiB) | 51 | DeepSeek-V3.1 (FP8) | 16xH20 TP16 | 1.17s | 10.19s (5.39GiB) | 11.80s (5.41GiB) | 52 | Kimi-K2-Instruct (FP8) | 16xH20 TP16 | 1.33s | 14.36s (5.89GiB) | 17.49s (5.91GiB) | 53 | DeepSeek-V3.1 (FP8) | 256xH20 TP16 | 0.80s | 11.33s (8.00GiB) | 11.81s (8.00GiB) | 54 | Kimi-K2-Instruct (FP8) | 256xH20 TP16 | 1.22s | 16.04s (8.00GiB) | 16.75s (8.00GiB) | 55 56 All results above are tested by [`examples/update.py`](./examples/update.py) and use [vLLM v0.10.2rc1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/v0.10.2rc1) as inference engine. Some notes: 57 58 * FP8 test needs additional vLLM patches, see [FP8 quantization](#fp8-quantization). 59 * Device Info: we tested various combination of devices and parallelism setups. For example, a 256-GPU TP16 setup means that we deploy 16 vLLM instances, each with 16-way tensor parallelism. 60 * Since update duration is related to IPC bucket size, we provide the bucket size in the table. 61 * The P2P time were tested for updating no more than two nodes (16 GPUs) (`ParameterServer.update(ranks=range(0, 16))`) out of the entire cluster. 62 * We bind each GPU to its corresponding NUMA node to ensure stable H2D transfer speeds. 63 64 ## Installation 65 66 Use the fastest broadcast implementation 67 68 ```Bash 69 pip install checkpoint-engine 70 ``` 71 72 Use the flexible P2P implementation, notice this will install `mooncake-transfer-engine` to support RDMA transfer between different ranks. 73 74 ```Bash 75 pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' 76 ``` 77 78 ### Intel XPU (build from source) 79 80 Intel XPU is supported for the **broadcast** update path. The cross-process weight handoff uses a native SYCL `ipc_memory` extension (the XPU counterpart of CUDA IPC) that is JIT-compiled at runtime. Install from source since XPU support is not yet in the released package. P2P is not supported on XPU (Mooncake has no Level Zero backend for XPU device memory). 81 82 Requirements: 83 - Intel XPU build of PyTorch — `torch.xpu.is_available()` returns `True`, `torch>=2.9` (for the device `.uuid` property; the SYCL extension build also needs `torch>=2.7`). See the [PyTorch XPU install guide](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/get_start_xpu.html); this is not the default PyPI `torch`. 84 - Intel oneAPI 2026.0+ providing the `icpx` compiler with SYCL IPC memory support. Needed at runtime (first weight update), not at `pip install` time. 85 86 ```Bash 87 git clone https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine.git 88 cd checkpoint-engine 89 pip install -e . # no [p2p] extra on XPU 90 ``` 91 92 Make `icpx` discoverable in the runtime environment, either by sourcing oneAPI (`source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh`) or by setting `CMPLR_ROOT`. If neither is set, `icpx` is auto-detected under `/opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/*/bin` and then on `PATH`. The extension then builds automatically on first use; `ParameterServer` also prebuilds it at startup so the one-time compile stays out of the update window. 93 94 Verify the build and the IPC path on the target machine: 95 96 ```Bash 97 pytest tests/test_xpu_ipc.py # hardware-gated; skipped without an Intel GPU + buildable extension 98 ``` 99 100 ## Getting Started 101 102 Prepare an H800 or H20 machine with 8 GPUs with vLLM. Be sure to include [/collective_rpc API endpoint](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f7cf5b512ee41f36613deb2471a44de5f304f70d) commit (available in main branch) since checkpoint-engine will use this endpoint to update weights. vLLM version `v0.10.2` is fully tested and recommended. 103 104 ```Bash 105 mkdir -p /opt/vLLM && cd /opt/vLLM 106 uv venv --python 3.12 --seed 107 source .venv/bin/activate 108 uv pip install vllm==0.10.2 109 ``` 110 111 Install checkpoint-engine 112 113 ```Bash 114 uv pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' 115 ``` 116 117 We use `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507` (BF16) as the test model 118 119 ```Bash 120 hf download Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 --local-dir /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ 121 ``` 122 123 Start vLLM in dev mode and set `--load-format dummy`. Notice that we also set `--worker-extension-cls=checkpoint_engine.worker.VllmColocateWorkerExtension` 124 125 ```Bash 126 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 19730 --trust-remote-code \ 127 --tensor-parallel-size=8 --max-model-len 4096 --load-format dummy \ 128 --served-model-name checkpoint-engine-demo --model /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ \ 129 --worker-extension-cls checkpoint_engine.worker.VllmColocateWorkerExtension 130 ``` 131 132 Meanwhile, use this command to update weights by checkpoint-engine. No need to wait for vLLM to get ready. 133 134 ```Bash 135 torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --update-method all --checkpoint-path /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ 136 ``` 137 138 ### Reuse weights from existing instances 139 140 New checkpoint-engine instances can join existing instances and reuse their weights. This is simple to achieve. 141 142 First, start the existing instances with `--save-metas-file global_metas.pkl` to save global metas to a file and use `--sleep-time 300` to make sure they stay alive. 143 144 ```Bash 145 torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --checkpoint-path $MODEL_PATH \ 146 --sleep-time 300 --save-metas-file global_metas.pkl 147 ``` 148 149 After a checkpoint is registered, new instances can obtain a copy of the checkpoint by setting `--load-metas-file global_metas.pkl`. 150 151 ```Bash 152 torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --load-metas-file global_metas.pkl 153 ``` 154 155 ### FP8 quantization 156 157 FP8 quantization currently do not natively work in vLLM when updating weights. 158 We provide a simple patch in [`patches/vllm_fp8.patch`](./patches/vllm_fp8.patch) to handle the correct weight update. 159 Notice this patch is only tested in DeepSeek-V3.1 and Kimi-K2. Other models may meet some compatible issues. 160 161 A [PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24488) is opened to the vLLM project and waiting to discuss and review. 162 163 ### Test 164 165 Run a simple correctness test for checkpoint_engine 166 167 ```bash 168 pytest tests/test_update.py 169 ``` 170 171 `test_update.py` are only designed to run with `pytest`. Please don't run it directly with `torchrun`. 172 173 Other unit tests can also be done with pytest. Only test_update.py requires GPUs, other tests can be run on CPUs. Only to run CPU tests, use: 174 175 ```bash 176 pytest tests/ -m "not gpu" 177 ``` 178 179 ### Environment Variables 180 - `PS_MAX_BUCKET_SIZE_GB`: An integer is used to set the maximum bucket size for checkpoint-engine. If not set, 8GB is used as default. 181 - `PS_P2P_STORE_RDMA_DEVICES`: Comma-separated RDMA devices' names for P2P transfer. If not set, checkpoint-engine will fall back to use `NCCL_IB_HCA` to detect RDMA devices. 182 - `NCCL_IB_HCA`: Available patterns can be found from [NCCL documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/env.html#id8). If also not set, all RDMA devices will be used and divided evenly among the ranks. 183 184 ## SGLang Integration 185 186 Checkpoint Engine provides efficient distributed checkpoint loading for SGLang inference servers, significantly reducing model loading time for large models and multi-node setups. 187 188 ### Quick Start 189 190 **1. Install checkpoint-engine:** 191 ```bash 192 pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' 193 ``` 194 195 **2. Launch SGLang server:** 196 ```bash 197 python -m sglang.launch_server \ 198 --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ 199 --tp 8 \ 200 --load-format dummy \ 201 --wait-for-initial-weights 202 ``` 203 204 **3. Run checkpoint engine:** 205 ```bash 206 python -m sglang.srt.checkpoint_engine.update \ 207 --update-method broadcast \ 208 --checkpoint-path $MODEL_PATH \ 209 --inference-parallel-size 8 210 ``` 211 212 ### Multi-Node Setup 213 214 For 2-node setup, run the same commands on both nodes with appropriate `--host` and distributed training parameters. 215 216 ### Key Options 217 218 **SGLang Server:** 219 - `--wait-for-initial-weights`: Wait for checkpoint engine before becoming ready 220 - `--load-format dummy`: Enable overlapping initialization tasks 221 222 **Checkpoint Engine:** 223 - `--update-method`: Choose `broadcast`, `p2p`, or `all` 224 - `--inference-parallel-size`: Number of parallel processes 225 - `--checkpoint-path`: Model checkpoint directory 226 227 ## Limitations and Future Work 228 229 - This project is currently tested with vLLM and SGLang. Integration with other frameworks is planned for future releases. 230 - The perfect three-stage pipeline mentioned in our paper is currently not implemented. This could be useful for architectures where H2D and broadcast do not conflict in PCIE. 231 232 ## Acknowledgments 233 234 This open source project uses the same vLLM interface in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24295 . Thanks for the comments and insights from [youkaichao](https://github.com/youkaichao). 235

To minimize the overall transfer time, checkpoint-engine optimizes the bucket assignment for each sender-receiver pair. The optimization goal is to make full use of the available network bandwidth for each sender and receiver. See [issue #25](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine/issues/25) ## Benchmark | Model | Device Info | GatherMetas | Update (Broadcast) | Update (P2P) | | :----------------------------------- | :----------- | :---------- |:-------------------| :---------------------- | | GLM-4.5-Air (BF16) | 8xH800 TP8 | 0.12s | 3.47s (3.02GiB) | 4.12s (3.02GiB) | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 (BF16) | 8xH800 TP8 | 0.33s | 6.22s (2.67GiB) | 7.10s (2.68GiB) | | DeepSeek-V3.1 (FP8) | 16xH20 TP16 | 1.17s | 10.19s (5.39GiB) | 11.80s (5.41GiB) | | Kimi-K2-Instruct (FP8) | 16xH20 TP16 | 1.33s | 14.36s (5.89GiB) | 17.49s (5.91GiB) | | DeepSeek-V3.1 (FP8) | 256xH20 TP16 | 0.80s | 11.33s (8.00GiB) | 11.81s (8.00GiB) | | Kimi-K2-Instruct (FP8) | 256xH20 TP16 | 1.22s | 16.04s (8.00GiB) | 16.75s (8.00GiB) | All results above are tested by [`examples/update.py`](./examples/update.py) and use [vLLM v0.10.2rc1](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/v0.10.2rc1) as inference engine. Some notes: * FP8 test needs additional vLLM patches, see [FP8 quantization](#fp8-quantization). * Device Info: we tested various combination of devices and parallelism setups. For example, a 256-GPU TP16 setup means that we deploy 16 vLLM instances, each with 16-way tensor parallelism. * Since update duration is related to IPC bucket size, we provide the bucket size in the table. * The P2P time were tested for updating no more than two nodes (16 GPUs) (`ParameterServer.update(ranks=range(0, 16))`) out of the entire cluster. * We bind each GPU to its corresponding NUMA node to ensure stable H2D transfer speeds. ## Installation Use the fastest broadcast implementation ```Bash pip install checkpoint-engine ``` Use the flexible P2P implementation, notice this will install `mooncake-transfer-engine` to support RDMA transfer between different ranks. ```Bash pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' ``` ### Intel XPU (build from source) Intel XPU is supported for the **broadcast** update path. The cross-process weight handoff uses a native SYCL `ipc_memory` extension (the XPU counterpart of CUDA IPC) that is JIT-compiled at runtime. Install from source since XPU support is not yet in the released package. P2P is not supported on XPU (Mooncake has no Level Zero backend for XPU device memory). Requirements: - Intel XPU build of PyTorch — `torch.xpu.is_available()` returns `True`, `torch>=2.9` (for the device `.uuid` property; the SYCL extension build also needs `torch>=2.7`). See the [PyTorch XPU install guide](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/get_start_xpu.html); this is not the default PyPI `torch`. - Intel oneAPI 2026.0+ providing the `icpx` compiler with SYCL IPC memory support. Needed at runtime (first weight update), not at `pip install` time. ```Bash git clone https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine.git cd checkpoint-engine pip install -e . # no [p2p] extra on XPU ``` Make `icpx` discoverable in the runtime environment, either by sourcing oneAPI (`source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh`) or by setting `CMPLR_ROOT`. If neither is set, `icpx` is auto-detected under `/opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/*/bin` and then on `PATH`. The extension then builds automatically on first use; `ParameterServer` also prebuilds it at startup so the one-time compile stays out of the update window. Verify the build and the IPC path on the target machine: ```Bash pytest tests/test_xpu_ipc.py # hardware-gated; skipped without an Intel GPU + buildable extension ``` ## Getting Started Prepare an H800 or H20 machine with 8 GPUs with vLLM. Be sure to include [/collective_rpc API endpoint](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f7cf5b512ee41f36613deb2471a44de5f304f70d) commit (available in main branch) since checkpoint-engine will use this endpoint to update weights. vLLM version `v0.10.2` is fully tested and recommended. ```Bash mkdir -p /opt/vLLM && cd /opt/vLLM uv venv --python 3.12 --seed source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install vllm==0.10.2 ``` Install checkpoint-engine ```Bash uv pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' ``` We use `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507` (BF16) as the test model ```Bash hf download Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 --local-dir /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ ``` Start vLLM in dev mode and set `--load-format dummy`. Notice that we also set `--worker-extension-cls=checkpoint_engine.worker.VllmColocateWorkerExtension` ```Bash VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 19730 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size=8 --max-model-len 4096 --load-format dummy \ --served-model-name checkpoint-engine-demo --model /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ \ --worker-extension-cls checkpoint_engine.worker.VllmColocateWorkerExtension ``` Meanwhile, use this command to update weights by checkpoint-engine. No need to wait for vLLM to get ready. ```Bash torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --update-method all --checkpoint-path /opt/models/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507/ ``` ### Reuse weights from existing instances New checkpoint-engine instances can join existing instances and reuse their weights. This is simple to achieve. First, start the existing instances with `--save-metas-file global_metas.pkl` to save global metas to a file and use `--sleep-time 300` to make sure they stay alive. ```Bash torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --checkpoint-path $MODEL_PATH \ --sleep-time 300 --save-metas-file global_metas.pkl ``` After a checkpoint is registered, new instances can obtain a copy of the checkpoint by setting `--load-metas-file global_metas.pkl`. ```Bash torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 examples/update.py --load-metas-file global_metas.pkl ``` ### FP8 quantization FP8 quantization currently do not natively work in vLLM when updating weights. We provide a simple patch in [`patches/vllm_fp8.patch`](./patches/vllm_fp8.patch) to handle the correct weight update. Notice this patch is only tested in DeepSeek-V3.1 and Kimi-K2. Other models may meet some compatible issues. A [PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24488) is opened to the vLLM project and waiting to discuss and review. ### Test Run a simple correctness test for checkpoint_engine ```bash pytest tests/test_update.py ``` `test_update.py` are only designed to run with `pytest`. Please don't run it directly with `torchrun`. Other unit tests can also be done with pytest. Only test_update.py requires GPUs, other tests can be run on CPUs. Only to run CPU tests, use: ```bash pytest tests/ -m "not gpu" ``` ### Environment Variables - `PS_MAX_BUCKET_SIZE_GB`: An integer is used to set the maximum bucket size for checkpoint-engine. If not set, 8GB is used as default. - `PS_P2P_STORE_RDMA_DEVICES`: Comma-separated RDMA devices' names for P2P transfer. If not set, checkpoint-engine will fall back to use `NCCL_IB_HCA` to detect RDMA devices. - `NCCL_IB_HCA`: Available patterns can be found from [NCCL documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/env.html#id8). If also not set, all RDMA devices will be used and divided evenly among the ranks. ## SGLang Integration Checkpoint Engine provides efficient distributed checkpoint loading for SGLang inference servers, significantly reducing model loading time for large models and multi-node setups. ### Quick Start **1. Install checkpoint-engine:** ```bash pip install 'checkpoint-engine[p2p]' ``` **2. Launch SGLang server:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path $MODEL_PATH \ --tp 8 \ --load-format dummy \ --wait-for-initial-weights ``` **3. Run checkpoint engine:** ```bash python -m sglang.srt.checkpoint_engine.update \ --update-method broadcast \ --checkpoint-path $MODEL_PATH \ --inference-parallel-size 8 ``` ### Multi-Node Setup For 2-node setup, run the same commands on both nodes with appropriate `--host` and distributed training parameters. ### Key Options **SGLang Server:** - `--wait-for-initial-weights`: Wait for checkpoint engine before becoming ready - `--load-format dummy`: Enable overlapping initialization tasks **Checkpoint Engine:** - `--update-method`: Choose `broadcast`, `p2p`, or `all` - `--inference-parallel-size`: Number of parallel processes - `--checkpoint-path`: Model checkpoint directory ## Limitations and Future Work - This project is currently tested with vLLM and SGLang. Integration with other frameworks is planned for future releases. - The perfect three-stage pipeline mentioned in our paper is currently not implemented. This could be useful for architectures where H2D and broadcast do not conflict in PCIE. ## Acknowledgments This open source project uses the same vLLM interface in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24295 . Thanks for the comments and insights from [youkaichao](https://github.com/youkaichao).

import argparse
import os

from loguru import logger

from checkpoint_engine.api import _init_api
from checkpoint_engine.ps import ParameterServer


@logger.catch(reraise=True)
def run_from_cli():
    import uvicorn

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Parameter Server")
    parser.add_argument("--uds", type=str)

    args = parser.parse_args()
    logger.info(
        f"Parameter Server {args=}, master addr: {os.getenv('MASTER_ADDR')}, master port {os.getenv('MASTER_PORT')}"
    )

    assert args.uds and len(args.uds) > 0, args.uds
    ps = ParameterServer(auto_pg=True)
    uvicorn.run(_init_api(ps), uds=args.uds, timeout_keep_alive=60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_from_cli()

2	from typing import Any
3	
4	import fastapi
5	import httpx
6	from fastapi import HTTPException, Request
7	from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response
8	from loguru import logger
9	from pydantic import BaseModel

11	from checkpoint_engine.data_types import MemoryBufferMetaList
12	from checkpoint_engine.ps import ParameterServer
13

15	def request_inference_to_update(
16	    url: str,
17	    socket_paths: dict[str, str],
18	    timeout: float = 300.0,
19	    uds: str | None = None,
20	):
21	    """Send an inference update request to inference server via HTTP or Unix socket.
22	
23	    Args:
24	        url (str): The HTTP URL or request path (e.g., "http://localhost:19730/inference") to send the request to.
25	        socket_paths (dict[str, str]): A dictionary containing device uuid and IPC socket paths for updating weights.
26	        timeout (float, optional): Request timeout in seconds. Defaults to 300.0.
27	        uds (str, optional): Path to a Unix domain socket. If provided, the request
28	            will be sent via the Unix socket instead of HTTP. Defaults to None.
29	
30	    Raises:
31	        httpx.HTTPStatusError: If the response contains an HTTP error status.
32	        httpx.RequestError: If there was an issue while making the request.
33	    """
34	    resp = httpx.Client(transport=httpx.HTTPTransport(uds=uds)).post(
35	        url,
36	        json={
37	            "method": "update_weights_from_ipc",
38	            "args": [socket_paths],
39	            "timeout": timeout,
40	        },
41	        timeout=timeout,
42	    )
43	    resp.raise_for_status()
44	
45	
46	def _init_api(ps: ParameterServer) -> Any:
47	    app = fastapi.FastAPI()
48	
49	    class RegisterRequest(BaseModel):
50	        files: list[str]
51	
52	    class UpdateRequest(BaseModel):
53	        ranks: list[int] = []
54	        update_url: str | None = None
55	        inference_group_ranks: list[int] = []
56	        timeout: float = 300.0
57	        uds: str | None = None
58	
59	    def wrap_exception(func: Callable[[], None]) -> Response:
60	        try:
61	            func()
62	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
63	            logger.exception(f"wrap exception {func} failed")
64	            return JSONResponse(content=str(e), status_code=500)
65	        return Response(status_code=200)
66	
67	    @app.post("/v1/checkpoints/{checkpoint_name}/files")
68	    async def register_files(checkpoint_name: str, req: RegisterRequest, raw: Request) -> Response:
69	        return wrap_exception(lambda: ps.register_checkpoint(checkpoint_name, files=req.files))
70	
71	    @app.delete("/v1/checkpoints/{checkpoint_name}")
72	    async def unregister_checkpoint(checkpoint_name: str) -> Response:
73	        return wrap_exception(lambda: ps.unregister_checkpoint(checkpoint_name))
74	
75	    @app.get("/v1/healthz")
76	    async def healthz() -> Response:
77	        return Response(status_code=200)
78	
79	    @app.post("/v1/checkpoints/{checkpoint_name}/gather-metas")
80	    async def gather_metas(checkpoint_name: str) -> Response:
81	        return wrap_exception(lambda: ps.gather_metas(checkpoint_name))
82	
83	    @app.get("/v1/metas")
84	    async def get_metas() -> dict[int, MemoryBufferMetaList]:
85	        try:
86	            return ps.get_metas()
87	        except Exception as e:
88	            logger.exception("get_metas failed")
89	            raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)) from e
90	
91	    @app.post("/v1/metas")
92	    async def load_metas(metas: dict[int, MemoryBufferMetaList]) -> Response:
93	        return wrap_exception(lambda: ps.load_metas(metas))
94	
95	    @app.post("/v1/checkpoints/{checkpoint_name}/update")
96	    async def update(checkpoint_name: str, req: UpdateRequest) -> Response:
97	        def update_func(socket_paths: list[tuple[str, str]]):
98	            if req.update_url is None:
99	                return
100	            if req.inference_group_ranks:
101	                socket_paths = [socket_paths[i] for i in req.inference_group_ranks]
102	            request_inference_to_update(
103	                req.update_url, dict(socket_paths), timeout=req.timeout, uds=req.uds
104	            )
105	
106	        return wrap_exception(lambda: ps.update(checkpoint_name, update_func, ranks=req.ranks))
107	
108	    return app

[project]
name = "checkpoint-engine"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "checkpoint-engine is a lightweight, decoupling and efficient weight update middleware"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

dependencies = [
    "torch>=2.5.0",
    "fastapi",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "safetensors",
    "pyzmq",
    "uvicorn",
    "loguru",
    "numpy",
    "httpx",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
p2p = [
    # `batch_register_memory` is introduced in 0.3.5
    "mooncake-transfer-engine>=0.3.5",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools-scm>=8"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["checkpoint_engine", "checkpoint_engine.*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# Ship the SYCL ipc_memory source; it is JIT-compiled at runtime on XPU hosts.
"checkpoint_engine.xpu_ipc" = ["*.cpp"]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_file = "checkpoint_engine/_version.py"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine"
Repository = "https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine"
Documentation = "https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine"
"Issue Tracker" = "https://github.com/MoonshotAI/checkpoint-engine/issues"

# Linter tools #################################################################

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 100
output-format = "full"
src = ["."]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
docstring-code-format = false
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W",  # pycodestyle
    "F",       # pyflakes
    "I",       # isort
    "N",       # pep8-naming
    "UP",      # pyupgrade
    "ANN",     # flake8-annotations
    "S",       # flake8-bandit
    "BLE",     # flake8-blind-except
    "B",       # flake8-bugbear
    "COM",     # flake8-commas
    "C4",      # flake8-comprehensions
    "EXE",     # flake8-executable
    "FA",      # flake8-future-annotations
    "ISC",     # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "LOG",     # flake8-logging
    "PIE",     # flake8-pie
    "PYI",     # flake8-pyi
    "Q",       # flake8-quotes
    "RSE",     # flake8-raise
    "SIM",     # flake8-simplify
    "TID",     # flake8-tidy-imports
    "TC",      # flake8-type-checking
    "PERF",    # perflint
    "FURB",    # refurb
    "TRY",     # tryceratops
    "RUF",     # ruff
    "ASYNC",   # flake8-async
]
ignore = [
    "ANN002",  # missing-type-args
    "ANN003",  # missing-type-kwargs
    "ANN204",  # missing-return-type-special-method
    "ANN401",  # any-type
    "B027",    # empty-method-without-abstract-decorator
    "B905",    # zip-without-explicit-strict, we use `zip-strict-fixer` instead
    "C416",    # unnecessary-comprehension
    "COM812",  # missing-trailing-comma
    "E501",    # line-too-long
    "N802",    # invalid-function-name
    "RUF005",  # collection-literal-concatenation
    "S101",    # assert
    "S105",    # hardcoded-password-string
    "S106",    # hardcoded-password-func-arg
    "S107",    # hardcoded-password-default
    "S301",    # suspicious-pickle-usage
    "S311",    # suspicious-non-cryptographic-random-usage
    "SIM105",  # suppressible-exception
    "SIM108",  # if-else-block-instead-of-if-exp
    "TID252",  # relative-imports
    "TRY003",  # raise-vanilla-args
    "TRY400",  # error-instead-of-exception
    "W505",    # doc-line-too-long
]
allowed-confusables = ["，", "。", "：", "？", "！", "、", "（", "）", "；", "“", "”"]
extend-safe-fixes = [
    "C408",     # unnecessary-collection-call
    "E711",     # none-comparison
    "FURB129",  # readlines-in-for
    "PERF102",  # incorrect-dict-iterator
    "PIE810",   # multiple-starts-ends-with
    "SIM102",   # collapsible-if
    "TC001",    # typing-only-first-party-import
    "TC002",    # typing-only-third-party-import
    "TC003",    # typing-only-standard-library-import
    "TC004",    # runtime-import-in-type-checking-block
    "TRY201",   # verbose-raise
    "UP004",    # useless-object-inheritance
    "UP008",    # super-call-with-parameters
    "UP038",    # non-pep604-isinstance
    "UP039",    # unnecessary-class-parentheses
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = [
    "F401",    # unused-import
    "TID252",  # relative-imports
]
"test/**/*.py" = [
    "ANN",
    "S108",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["checkpoint_engine"]
known-local-folder = ["checkpoint_engine", "tests"]
lines-after-imports = 2

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-annotations]
allow-star-arg-any = true
suppress-dummy-args = true
suppress-none-returning = true


[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel"]
runtime-evaluated-decorators = ["pydantic.validate_call"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-quotes]
docstring-quotes = "double"
multiline-quotes = "double"
inline-quotes = "double"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "gpu: marks tests as GPU test (deselect with '-m \"not gpu\"')",
]

52	    try:
53	        if device_manager.device_type == "npu":

68	def _gen_h2d_buckets(
69	    global_metas: dict[int, MemoryBufferMetaList],
70	    bucket_size: int,
71	    local_topo: dict[str, set[int]],
72	    remote_topo: dict[str, set[int]],
73	    ranks: list[int] | None = None,
74	) -> list[tuple[int, int, H2DBucket]]:
75	    buckets: list[tuple[int, H2DBucket]] = []
76	
77	    for owner_rank, items in global_metas.items():
78	        buckets.append((owner_rank, H2DBucket(size=0, ranges=[], items=[])))
79	        for idx, metas in enumerate(items.memory_buffer_metas_list):
80	            start_offset, offset = 0, 0
81	            for meta in metas.metas:
82	                s = meta.aligned_size
83	                if buckets[-1][1].size + s > bucket_size:
84	                    if offset - start_offset > 0:
85	                        buckets[-1][1].ranges.append(
86	                            BucketRange(idx, start_offset, offset - start_offset)
87	                        )
88	                    start_offset = offset
89	                    buckets.append((owner_rank, H2DBucket(size=0, ranges=[], items=[])))
90	                offset += s
91	                buckets[-1][1].size += s
92	                buckets[-1][1].items.append(meta)
93	            buckets[-1][1].ranges.append(BucketRange(idx, start_offset, offset - start_offset))
94	        assert buckets[-1][1].size > 0, (
95	            f"buckets[-1][1].size {buckets[-1][1].size} should be greater than 0"
96	        )
97	    ranks_set = set(ranks) if ranks else set()
98	    actual_local_topo = (
99	        {k: v & ranks_set for k, v in local_topo.items() if v & ranks_set} if ranks else local_topo
100	    )
101	    # if ranks is empty, assign the owner_rank as receiver_rank, this is used for colocate architecture
102	    if not ranks:
103	        return [(owner_rank, owner_rank, bucket) for owner_rank, bucket in buckets]
104	    else:
105	        return _assign_receiver_ranks(buckets, actual_local_topo, remote_topo)

107	
108	def _assign_receiver_ranks(
109	    buckets: list[tuple[int, "T"]],
110	    local_topo: dict[str, set[int]],
111	    remote_topo: dict[str, set[int]],
112	) -> list[tuple[int, int, "T"]]:
113	    """
114	    (owner_rank, bucket) -> (receiver_rank, owner_rank, bucket)
115	
116	    Assign receiver ranks to buckets. If ranks is empty, assign the owner_rank as receiver_rank.
117	    GPU-rdma_device topology will be considered to make full use of the bandwidth.
118	    """
119	    if not buckets:
120	        logger.warning("bucket list is empty, no need to assign receiver ranks")
121	        return []
122	    rank_to_rdma_device = {
123	        rank: rdma_device for rdma_device, ranks in remote_topo.items() for rank in ranks
124	    }
125	
126	    # group buckets by owner RDMA devices
127	    buckets_by_rdma_device = defaultdict(list)
128	    for owner_rank, bucket in buckets:
129	        owner_rdma_device = rank_to_rdma_device[owner_rank]
130	        buckets_by_rdma_device[owner_rdma_device].append((owner_rank, bucket))
131	
132	    buckets_matrix = list(buckets_by_rdma_device.values())
133	    assert buckets_matrix, "buckets_matrix should not be empty"
134	
135	    # Select receiver ranks. We use the minimum rank in each local RDMA device group as receiver rank
136	    num_receivers = min(len(local_topo), len(buckets_by_rdma_device))
137	    receiver_list = [min(ranks) for ranks in list(local_topo.values())[:num_receivers]]
138	
139	    flattened_buckets = [
140	        buckets_matrix[row][col]
141	        for col in range(
142	            max(len(matrix_row) for matrix_row in buckets_matrix) if buckets_matrix else 0
143	        )
144	        for row in range(len(buckets_matrix))
145	        if col < len(buckets_matrix[row])
146	    ]
147	
148	    buckets_with_receiver = []
149	    assigned_cnt = 0
150	    while assigned_cnt < len(flattened_buckets):
151	        occupied_devices = set()
152	        for receiver_rank in receiver_list:
153	            if assigned_cnt >= len(flattened_buckets):
154	                break
155	            owner_rank, bucket = flattened_buckets[assigned_cnt]
156	            rdma_device = rank_to_rdma_device[owner_rank]
157	            if rdma_device in occupied_devices:
158	                break
159	            buckets_with_receiver.append((receiver_rank, owner_rank, bucket))
160	            occupied_devices.add(rdma_device)
161	            assigned_cnt += 1
162	
163	    return buckets_with_receiver

179	    def __init__(
180	        self,
181	        *,
182	        rank: int | None = None,
183	        world_size: int | None = None,
184	        auto_pg: bool = True,
185	        gpu_count: int | None = None,
186	        mem_fraction: float | None = None,

190	        """
191	        Initialize the parameter server. env RANK, WORLD_SIZE and MASTER_ADDR must be set.
192	
193	        Args:
194	            auto_pg: Whether to automatically initialize the process group.
195	                Notice that if auto_pg is True, will destroy the process group after update. It is recommended to set auto_pg to True!

197	        """

199	        self._world_size = world_size or int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
200	        self.device_manager = DeviceManager()
201	        self._gpu_count = gpu_count or self.device_manager.device_module.device_count()
202	        self._local_rank = self._rank % self._gpu_count
203	        self._auto_pg = auto_pg

206	        self._local_rdma_devices: dict[str, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
207	        self._remote_rdma_devices: dict[str, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
208	        self._mem_fraction = mem_fraction or float(os.getenv("PS_MEM_FRACTION", "0.9"))
209	
210	        assert self._rank is not None and self._rank >= 0, self._rank
211	        assert self._world_size and self._world_size > 0, self._world_size
212	        assert (
213	            self._gpu_count is not None
214	            and self._gpu_count > 0
215	            and self._gpu_count <= self.device_manager.device_module.device_count()
216	        ), self._gpu_count
217	        assert (

219	        ), self._mem_fraction

221	        self._zmq_ctx = zmq.Context()
222	        self._zmq_addr_counter = 0

224	        # stores the name of the checkpoint currently using the shared memory pool, or empty string if none
225	        self._current_shared_memory_pool_user: str = ""
226	        self._memory_pool: dict[str, list[MemoryBuffer]] = {}
227	        self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name] = []
228	        # dict key is owner_rank, value is a bucket metas list in owner_rank
229	        self._current_global_parameter_metas: dict[int, MemoryBufferMetaList] = {}
230	        # NPU transfer engine initialization requires prior set_device.
231	        device_index = self._local_rank
232	        self.device_manager.device_module.set_device(device_index)
233	        # P2P (Mooncake) transfer is only supported on CUDA/NPU; XPU has no Level Zero
234	        # backend for device memory. Skip the store entirely on unsupported backends
235	        # rather than eagerly initializing something that can never be used (and whose
236	        # engine.initialize() may fail with more than just ImportError).
237	        if self.device_manager.supports_device_p2p():
238	            try:

240	            except ImportError as e:
241	                logger.warning(f"[rank{self._rank}] fail to initialize p2p store due to {e}")
242	                self._p2p_store = None

245	                f"[rank{self._rank}] p2p store disabled: not supported on device type "
246	                f"'{self.device_manager.device_type}'"
247	            )
248	            self._p2p_store = None

250	        self._device_uuid = _get_physical_gpu_id(self.device_manager, device_index)
251	        self._rdma_device = None if self._p2p_store is None else self._p2p_store.device
252	
253	        # Build the JIT SYCL IPC extension now, so its multi-second compile is outside
254	        # the first weight-update window.
255	        if self.device_manager.device_type == "xpu":
256	            from checkpoint_engine import xpu_ipc
257	
258	            if xpu_ipc.prewarm():
259	                logger.info(f"[rank{self._rank}] XPU SYCL ipc_memory extension prebuilt")
260	            else:

264	                )

266	        master_addr = master_addr or os.getenv("MASTER_ADDR")

277	    def _get_memory_pool(self, checkpoint_name: str) -> list[MemoryBuffer]:

281	            )

296	        self._current_global_parameter_metas = metas

298	        for i, meta in self._current_global_parameter_metas.items():
299	            assert meta.rdma_device is not None, "meta.rdma_device should not be None"

303	            ].add(i)
304	
305	    def register_checkpoint(
306	        self,
307	        checkpoint_name: str,
308	        *,
309	        files: list[str] | None = None,
310	        named_tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
311	        use_shared_memory_pool: bool = False,
312	        use_inplace_pin_memory: bool = True,
313	    ) -> None:
314	        """
315	        Register a checkpoint to the parameter server. Both files and named_tensors will be registered together.
316	        Warning: if `use_inplace_pin_memory` is True, .safetensors files in /dev/shm/ will be pinned in-place, and the files will be REMOVED after pinning.
317	        Please make sure to copy the files to disks if you need to keep them. NPU does not support inplace pin memory.
318	
319	        Args:
320	            checkpoint_name: The name of the checkpoint.
321	            files: The safetensors files to register.
322	            named_tensors: The named tensors to register.
323	            use_shared_memory_pool: If True, uses a reusable shared pin memory pool instead of allocating new memory.
324	                Only one checkpoint can use the shared pool at a time. The pool's shape is fixed on first use and
325	                cannot accommodate checkpoints with different memory requirements.
326	                To free the actual memory of the shared pool or to modify its shape,
327	                please unregister the current user of the shared memory pool using `unregister_checkpoint` with `force=True`.
328	            use_inplace_pin_memory: If True (default), allows inplace pin memory for /dev/shm/ safetensors files.
329	                This option is ignored when ``use_shared_memory_pool`` is True.
330	        """
331	        if not self.device_manager.supports_inplace_pin() and use_inplace_pin_memory:
332	            logger.warning(
333	                f"[rank{self._rank}] Only cuda devices support in-place pin memory, set use_inplace_pin_memory to False"
334	            )
335	            use_inplace_pin_memory = False
336	        try:
337	            if use_shared_memory_pool:
338	                logger.info(
339	                    f"[rank{self._rank}] checkpoint {checkpoint_name} use shared memory pool"
340	                )
341	                assert self._current_shared_memory_pool_user == "", (
342	                    f"cannot register checkpoint {checkpoint_name} to shared memory pool, "
343	                    f"since checkpoint {self._current_shared_memory_pool_user} is already using shared memory pool. "
344	                    f"This registration may cause unexpected conflicts."
345	                )
346	                # Since we set the uninitialized shared memory pool to empty list,
347	                # we can check whether this is the first time to use shared memory pool
348	                _is_first_time = not self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name]
349	                self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name] = _register_checkpoint(
350	                    files=files or [],
351	                    named_tensors=named_tensors or {},
352	                    rank=self._rank,
353	                    shared_pin_memory=self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name],
354	                    inplace_pin=False,  # inplace pin memory is not compatible with shared memory pool
355	                )
356	                self._current_shared_memory_pool_user = checkpoint_name
357	                if self._p2p_store is not None and _is_first_time:
358	                    self._register_parameters_to_p2p_store(checkpoint_name)
359	            else:
360	                assert checkpoint_name not in self._memory_pool, (
361	                    f"checkpoint {checkpoint_name} already registered"
362	                )
363	                self._memory_pool[checkpoint_name] = _register_checkpoint(
364	                    files=files or [],
365	                    named_tensors=named_tensors or {},
366	                    rank=self._rank,
367	                    inplace_pin=use_inplace_pin_memory,
368	                )
369	                if self._p2p_store is not None:
370	                    self._register_parameters_to_p2p_store(checkpoint_name)
371	        except Exception:
372	            logger.exception(
373	                f"[rank{self._rank}] fail to register checkpoint {checkpoint_name} with files {files}"
374	            )
375	            if self._p2p_store is not None and not use_shared_memory_pool:
376	                self._unregister_parameters_from_p2p_store(checkpoint_name)
377	            self.unregister_checkpoint(checkpoint_name)
378	            raise

380	    def unregister_checkpoint(self, checkpoint_name: str, force: bool = False) -> None:
381	        """
382	        Unregister a checkpoint from the parameter server. This function will also unregister the checkpoint
383	        from p2p store if p2p store is initialized.
384	        Args:
385	            checkpoint_name: The name of the checkpoint.
386	            force: This flag is designed for shared memory pool user. If True, the memory for shared memory pool itself will be freed.
387	                    If False, only the checkpoint name will be unregistered, and the shared memory pool will be kept for future use.
388	        """
389	        if (
390	            checkpoint_name not in self._memory_pool
391	            and checkpoint_name != self._current_shared_memory_pool_user
392	        ):
393	            logger.warning(
394	                f"[rank{self._rank}] unregister checkpoint name {checkpoint_name} not found"
395	            )
396	            return
397	
398	        if checkpoint_name == self._current_shared_memory_pool_user and not force:
399	            self._current_shared_memory_pool_user = ""
400	            return
401	
402	        if self._p2p_store is not None:
403	            num_unregistered = self._unregister_parameters_from_p2p_store(checkpoint_name)
404	            logger.info(
405	                f"[rank{self._rank}] unregister {num_unregistered} parameters from p2p store for checkpoint {checkpoint_name}"
406	            )
407	
408	        if checkpoint_name == self._current_shared_memory_pool_user:
409	            self._current_shared_memory_pool_user = ""
410	            del self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name]
411	            self._memory_pool[self.shared_memory_pool_name] = []
412	        else:
413	
414	            def _unpin(t: torch.Tensor):
415	                """
416	                Un-pin the pinned memory.
417	                """
418	                p_flags = ctypes.c_uint()
419	                try:
420	                    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None)  # get all symbols from the current process
421	                    cuda_host_get_flags = libc.cudaHostGetFlags
422	                    cuda_host_get_flags.argtypes = [ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_uint), ctypes.c_void_p]
423	                    cuda_host_get_flags.restype = ctypes.c_int
424	                except AttributeError:
425	                    logger.error("cudaHostGetFlags not found in libc, cannot unpin memory manually")
426	                    raise
427	                r = cuda_host_get_flags(ctypes.byref(p_flags), ctypes.c_void_p(t.data_ptr()))
428	                assert r == 0, f"get pin flags error, error code: {r}"
429	                # p_flags value meaning from cuda/include/driver_types.h
430	                # cudaHostRegisterDefault             0x00  /**< Default host memory registration flag */
431	                # cudaHostRegisterPortable            0x01  /**< Pinned memory accessible by all CUDA contexts */
432	                # cudaHostRegisterMapped              0x02  /**< Map registered memory into device space */
433	                # cudaHostRegisterIoMemory            0x04  /**< Memory-mapped I/O space */
434	                # cudaHostRegisterReadOnly            0x08  /**< Memory-mapped read-only */
435	                assert p_flags.value == 0x02, (
436	                    f"pin memory flag error, expected: 0x02 (cudaHostRegisterMapped), got flag: {p_flags.value}"
437	                )
438	                cudart = torch.cuda.cudart()
439	                r = cudart.cudaHostUnregister(t.data_ptr())
440	                if r != 0:
441	                    error_msg = cudart.cudaGetErrorString(r)
442	                    raise RuntimeError(
443	                        f"unpin memory error, error code: {r}, error message: {error_msg}"
444	                    )
445	
446	            # if the checkpoint is pinned by cudaHostRegister manually, we need to unpin it manually
447	            try:
448	                for memory_buffer in self._memory_pool.get(checkpoint_name, []):
449	                    if memory_buffer.manually_pinned:
450	                        _unpin(memory_buffer.buffer)
451	            except Exception as e:
452	                logger.error(
453	                    f"[rank{self._rank}] fail to unpin memory for checkpoint {checkpoint_name}: {e}"
454	                )
455	                raise
456	            # we won't delete the memory pool if unpinning fails.
457	            del self._memory_pool[checkpoint_name]
458	        # see https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/31d5c675394705f8a6bc767f80ae14bf4f01246b/torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp#L2018
459	        # this works by using torch>=2.5.0 on cuda; NPU/XPU fall back to gc.collect().
460	        self.device_manager.host_empty_cache()

462	    def gather_metas(self, checkpoint_name: str):
463	        """
464	        Gather the parameter metas from all ranks. This will gather memory_buffer, and other metadatas.
465	        This function should be called before update and init a new value to `self._current_global_parameter_metas`,
466	        which can be exported by using `self.get_metas` function.
467	        """
468	        if self._auto_pg and not dist.is_initialized():
469	            self.init_process_group()
470	        assert dist.is_initialized(), "process group is not initialized"
471	        metas_lst: list[DataToGather | None] = [None for _ in range(self._world_size)]  # type: ignore
472	        try:
473	            memory_pool = self._get_memory_pool(checkpoint_name)
474	        except RuntimeError:
475	            memory_pool = []
476	        metas = DataToGather(
477	            memory_buffer_metas_list=[
478	                MemoryBufferMetas(
479	                    metas=x.metas,
480	                    ptr=x.buffer.data_ptr(),
481	                    size=x.size,
482	                )
483	                for x in memory_pool
484	            ],
485	            p2p_store_addr=None if self._p2p_store is None else self._p2p_store.addr,
486	            host_ip=get_ip(),
487	            device_uuid=self._device_uuid,
488	            rdma_device=self._rdma_device or "",
489	        )
490	
491	        dist.all_gather_object(metas_lst, metas)
492	
493	        self._current_global_parameter_metas = {}
494	
495	        num_parameters = 0
496	        all_hosts: list[str] = []
497	        global_device_uuids: list[str] = []
498	        for i, metas_buckets in enumerate(metas_lst):
499	            assert metas_buckets is not None, f"metas_buckets {i} should not be None"
500	            if i % self._gpu_count == 0 and not self._all_hosts:
501	                all_hosts.append(metas_buckets.host_ip)
502	            if not self._global_device_uuids:
503	                global_device_uuids.append(metas_buckets.device_uuid)
504	            if metas_buckets.memory_buffer_metas_list:
505	                self._current_global_parameter_metas[i] = MemoryBufferMetaList(
506	                    memory_buffer_metas_list=metas_buckets.memory_buffer_metas_list,
507	                    p2p_store_addr=metas_buckets.p2p_store_addr,
508	                    rdma_device=metas_buckets.rdma_device,
509	                )
510	                num_parameters += sum(len(x.metas) for x in metas_buckets.memory_buffer_metas_list)
511	            self._local_rdma_devices[
512	                metas_buckets.rdma_device + "@" + metas_buckets.p2p_store_addr.split(":")[0]
513	                if metas_buckets.p2p_store_addr
514	                else metas_buckets.host_ip
515	            ].add(i)
516	        if not self._all_hosts:
517	            self._all_hosts = all_hosts
518	        if not self._global_device_uuids:
519	            self._global_device_uuids = global_device_uuids
520	        # Sender node and Receiver node have the same GPU-rdma_device topology is considered as default.
521	        # Rewrite the sender's topology (_remote_rdma_devices) by calling load_metas.
522	        self._remote_rdma_devices = self._local_rdma_devices.copy()
523	        logger.info(
524	            f"[rank{self._rank}] gather parameter metas finished, num_parameters: {num_parameters}"
525	        )

527	    def init_process_group(
528	        self,
529	        *,
530	        timeout: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=10),
531	    ):
532	        """
533	        Initialize the process group for the ranks. This global group can be easily destroyed by calling dist.destroy_process_group.
534	
535	        Args:
536	            master_port: The specified port of the master node. If not set, will use _get_master_port to get the port.
537	            timeout: The timeout of the process group.
538	        """
539	        self._store_counter += 1
540	        sub_store = torch.distributed.PrefixStore(f"prefix-{self._store_counter}", self._store)

543	            world_size=self._world_size,
544	            rank=self._rank,
545	            timeout=timeout,
546	            store=sub_store,

550	    def store_based_barrier(self, timeout: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=5)) -> None:
551	        """
552	        Perform a store-based barrier synchronization across all ranks.
553	
554	        This barrier uses a TCP store directly rather than a process group,
555	        allowing all ranks to synchronize regardless of which process group
556	        they belong to.
557	
558	        Args:
559	            store: The TCPStore instance to use for synchronization.
560	        """
561	        torch.distributed.distributed_c10d._store_based_barrier(
562	            rank=self._rank,
563	            store=self._store,
564	            group_name="parameter_server_barrier",
565	            rendezvous_count=self._world_size,
566	            timeout=timeout,
567	        )

569	    def update(
570	        self,
571	        checkpoint_name: str,
572	        req_func: Callable[[list[tuple[str, str]]], None],
573	        *,
574	        timeout: timedelta = timedelta(minutes=10),
575	        ranks: list[int] | None = None,
576	    ) -> None:
577	        """
578	        Update the checkpoint to inference engine. This function should be called after gather_metas.
579	        Warning: if _auto_pg is False when initializing ParameterServer, please make sure ALL ranks in the WORLD_SIZE call `update` function,
580	        otherwise, it will hang.
581	
582	        Args:
583	            checkpoint_name: The name of the checkpoint.
584	            req_func: The function to request the inference of inference engine.
585	            ranks: The ranks to update. If not set, will use fully broadcast to update to all ranks,
586	                which is the fastest way to update weights, especially in colocated architecture.
587	                If set, will use p2p to update to the ranks, this is flexible to update to a group of ranks,
588	                which is useful in disaggregated architecture.
589	            master_addr: The master address for process group initialization. If not set, will use env MASTER_ADDR.
590	            master_port: The master port for process group initialization. If not set, will use _get_master_port to get the port, which will use MASTER_PORT+1.
591	            timeout: The timeout of the barrier operation.
592	        """
593	        assert req_func is not None, "req_func is required"
594	        ranks_group = None
595	        try:
596	            if self._auto_pg and not dist.is_initialized():
597	                self.init_process_group(timeout=timeout)
598	            # if ranks is None or [], it will use fully broadcast to update to all ranks
599	            ranks_group = dist.new_group(ranks) if ranks else None
600	            # `with` releases the exported IPC handle on every exit path, including a
601	            # failure before the broadcast loop's own cleanup starts.
602	            with build_ipc_handler(self.device_manager) as ipc_handler:
603	                self._update_per_bucket(checkpoint_name, req_func, ipc_handler, ranks_group, ranks)
604	            self.store_based_barrier()
605	        except Exception as e:
606	            logger.exception(
607	                f"[rank{self._rank}] update checkpoint {checkpoint_name} with ranks {ranks} error {e}"
608	            )
609	            raise
610	        finally:
611	            if ranks_group:
612	                dist.destroy_process_group(ranks_group)
613	            if self._auto_pg and dist.is_initialized():
614	                dist.destroy_process_group()
615	            self.device_manager.device_module.empty_cache()
616	            logger.info(
617	                f"[rank{self._rank}] update checkpoint {checkpoint_name} with ranks {ranks} done. "
618	                f"Current device allocated {self.device_manager.device_module.memory_allocated() / 1024 / 1024} MB, "
619	                f"reserved {self.device_manager.device_module.memory_reserved() / 1024 / 1024} MB."
620	            )

622	    def _bind_zmq_socket(self) -> tuple[zmq.Socket, list[tuple[str, str]]]:
623	        def zmq_handle(device_uuid: str) -> str:
624	            return f"ipc://@checkpoint-engine-{device_uuid}-{self._zmq_addr_counter}.sock"
625	
626	        socket_paths = [(uid, zmq_handle(uid)) for uid in self._global_device_uuids]
627	        socket = self._zmq_ctx.socket(zmq.REQ)
628	        socket.bind(zmq_handle(self._device_uuid))
629	        self._zmq_addr_counter += 1
630	        return socket, socket_paths

632	    def _detect_bucket_size(
633	        self,
634	        ranks_group: dist.DistributedProcessGroup | None,
635	        *,
636	        disable_h2d_buffer: bool = False,
637	    ) -> tuple[int, bool]:
638	        GiB = 1 << 30  # noqa: N806
639	        # auto detect bucket size
640	        tensor = torch.tensor(
641	            [
642	                # proportion of current device free memory bytes
643	                int(
644	                    float(self.device_manager.device_module.mem_get_info()[0]) * self._mem_fraction
645	                ),
646	                # we use negative value to reuse allreduce min operation
647	                # for getting the max value of zmq_addr_counter in all ranks
648	                -self._zmq_addr_counter,
649	            ],
650	            dtype=torch.int64,
651	            device=self.device_manager.device_type,
652	        )
653	        dist.all_reduce(tensor, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, group=ranks_group)
654	        tensor = tensor.cpu()
655	        free_bytes, self._zmq_addr_counter = tensor[0].item(), -tensor[1].item()
656	        max_tensor_bytes = 0
657	        for items in self._current_global_parameter_metas.values():
658	            for metas_list in items.memory_buffer_metas_list:
659	                for meta in metas_list.metas:
660	                    max_tensor_bytes = max(max_tensor_bytes, meta.aligned_size)
661	        free_bytes_divided_3 = free_bytes // (3 * _ALIGN_SIZE) * _ALIGN_SIZE
662	        if max_tensor_bytes <= free_bytes_divided_3 and not disable_h2d_buffer:
663	            self._logger_rank0(f"[rank{self._rank}] use h2d buffer")
664	            # using h2d_buffer can make all ranks' h2d parallel execution
665	            # the cost is that we need to allocate extra h2d_buffer's GPU memory
666	            free_bytes = free_bytes_divided_3
667	        else:
668	            # if the memory is not enough, it will fallback to disable_h2d_buffer mode,
669	            # at this time, the bandwidth will be limited by the h2d of a single machine,
670	            # but we can save GPU memory
671	            self._logger_rank0(
672	                f"[rank{self._rank}] disable h2d buffer when max_tensor_bytes {max_tensor_bytes} is larger than free_bytes {free_bytes} // 3"
673	            )
674	            free_bytes = free_bytes // (2 * _ALIGN_SIZE) * _ALIGN_SIZE
675	            assert max_tensor_bytes <= free_bytes, (
676	                f"max_tensor_bytes {max_tensor_bytes} should be less than free_bytes {free_bytes}"
677	            )
678	            disable_h2d_buffer = True
679	        max_bytes = int(float(os.getenv("PS_MAX_BUCKET_SIZE_GB", "8")) * GiB)
680	        bucket_size = min(max(max_bytes, max_tensor_bytes), free_bytes)
681	        logger.info(f"[rank{self._rank}] auto detect bucket size {bucket_size / GiB:.2f} GiB")
682	        return bucket_size, disable_h2d_buffer

684	    def _copy_to_buffer(
685	        self,
686	        checkpoint_name: str,
687	        bucket: H2DBucket,
688	        buffer: torch.Tensor,
689	        owner_rank: int | None = None,
690	    ):
691	        offset = 0
692	        if owner_rank is not None:
693	            buf_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lens = [], [], []
694	            ptr_base = buffer.data_ptr()
695	            target_addr, ptrs = self._get_addr_ptrs(owner_rank)
696	        for b in bucket.ranges:
697	            assert offset + b.size <= bucket.size, (
698	                f"offset {offset} + size {b.size} > bucket_size {bucket.size}"
699	            )
700	            if owner_rank is not None:
701	                buf_ptrs.append(ptr_base + offset)
702	                remote_ptrs.append(ptrs[b.idx][0] + b.offset)
703	                lens.append(b.size)
704	            else:
705	                pool = self._get_memory_pool(checkpoint_name)[b.idx]
706	                buffer[offset : offset + b.size].data.copy_(
707	                    pool.buffer[b.offset : b.offset + b.size],
708	                    non_blocking=True,
709	                )
710	            offset += b.size
711	        assert offset == bucket.size, f"offset {offset} != bucket_size {bucket.size}"
712	        if owner_rank is not None:
713	            self._p2p_store.batch_transfer_sync_read(target_addr, buf_ptrs, remote_ptrs, lens)
714	        self.device_manager.device_module.synchronize()
715	
716	    def _get_addr_ptrs(self, owner_rank: int) -> tuple[str, list[tuple[int, int]]]:
717	        addr = self._current_global_parameter_metas[owner_rank].p2p_store_addr
718	        metas_list = self._current_global_parameter_metas[owner_rank].memory_buffer_metas_list
719	        return addr, [(metas.ptr, metas.size) for metas in metas_list]

721	    def _register_parameters_to_p2p_store(self, checkpoint_name: str):
722	        assert self._p2p_store is not None, "p2p store is not initialized"
723	        pool = self._get_memory_pool(checkpoint_name)
724	        if len(pool) == 0:
725	            return
726	        named_tensors, tensor_ptrs = {}, []
727	        register_name = (
728	            checkpoint_name
729	            if checkpoint_name != self._current_shared_memory_pool_user
730	            else self.shared_memory_pool_name
731	        )
732	        for idx, memory_buffer in enumerate(pool):
733	            named_tensors[f"memory_pool_{register_name}_{idx}"] = memory_buffer.buffer
734	            tensor_ptrs.append((memory_buffer.buffer.data_ptr(), memory_buffer.size))
735	        self._p2p_store.register_named_tensors(named_tensors)

737	    def _unregister_parameters_from_p2p_store(self, checkpoint_name: str) -> int:
738	        assert self._p2p_store is not None, "p2p store is not initialized"
739	        pool = self._get_memory_pool(checkpoint_name)
740	        if len(pool) == 0:
741	            return 0
742	        unregister_name = (
743	            checkpoint_name
744	            if checkpoint_name != self._current_shared_memory_pool_user
745	            else self.shared_memory_pool_name
746	        )
747	        return self._p2p_store.unregister_named_tensors(
748	            [f"memory_pool_{unregister_name}_{idx}" for idx, _ in enumerate(pool)]
749	        )

751	    def _update_per_bucket(
752	        self,
753	        checkpoint_name: str,
754	        req_func: Callable[[list[tuple[str, str]]], None],
755	        ipc_handler: IPCHandler,
756	        ranks_group: dist.DistributedProcessGroup | None,
757	        ranks: list[int] | None = None,
758	    ):
759	        assert len(self._current_global_parameter_metas) != 0, "parameter metas is empty"
760	        assert dist.is_initialized(), "process group is not initialized"
761	
762	        # The broadcast shares a device buffer with the colocated worker via cross-process
763	        # device-tensor IPC (CUDA/NPU: torch.multiprocessing; XPU: native SYCL ipc_memory).
764	        # Fail loudly here rather than with an opaque "_share_fd_: only available on CPU"
765	        # deeper in the update.
766	        if not self.device_manager.supports_device_ipc():
767	            raise RuntimeError(
768	                f"[rank{self._rank}] weight update requires cross-process device-tensor IPC, which "
769	                f"is not available for device type '{self.device_manager.device_type}' in this "
770	                f"environment. On XPU this needs the native SYCL ipc_memory extension "
771	                f"(an oneAPI 'icpx' compiler with SYCL ipc_memory support, i.e. oneAPI >= 2026.0)."
772	            )
773	
774	        p2p_update = False
775	        # if both ranks is None or [], it will use fully broadcast to update to all ranks
776	        if not ranks:
777	            logger.info(f"[rank{self._rank}] update checkpoint {checkpoint_name}")
778	        # if ranks is set, it will use p2p to update to the ranks
779	        else:
780	            # The P2P path RDMA-transfers device memory via Mooncake, which has no Level Zero
781	            # backend for XPU. Reject it clearly rather than failing inside p2p_store registration.
782	            if not self.device_manager.supports_device_p2p():
783	                raise RuntimeError(
784	                    f"[rank{self._rank}] P2P weight update (ranks={ranks}) is not supported on "
785	                    f"device type '{self.device_manager.device_type}': the Mooncake transfer engine "
786	                    f"cannot register {self.device_manager.device_type} device memory. Use the "
787	                    f"broadcast update (leave ranks unset) instead."
788	                )
789	            assert self._p2p_store is not None, "p2p store is not initialized"
790	            assert ranks, "ranks should be set"
791	
792	            p2p_update = True
793	            need_update = self._rank in ranks
794	            logger.info(
795	                f"[rank{self._rank}] update checkpoint {checkpoint_name} p2p, {need_update=} with {ranks=}, "
796	                f"gpu_count {self._gpu_count}, world_size {self._world_size}"
797	            )
798	
799	            if not need_update:
800	                return
801	            # first execute a barrier to avoid subsequent device oom
802	            dist.barrier(group=ranks_group)
803	
804	        bucket_size, disable_h2d_buffer = self._detect_bucket_size(ranks_group)
805	        buckets = _gen_h2d_buckets(
806	            self._current_global_parameter_metas,
807	            bucket_size,
808	            self._local_rdma_devices,
809	            self._remote_rdma_devices,
810	            ranks,
811	        )
812	
813	        h2d_buffer: torch.Tensor | None = (
814	            None
815	            if disable_h2d_buffer
